reason: The hypothesis makes several specific claims about thermodynamic stabilization, segregation mechanisms, and atmospheric effects, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these key premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers general concepts of entropy and enthalpy in alloys, but the specific application to equiatomic Co–Ni–Cu–Fe–Cr nanoparticles and the predicted behaviors require supporting citations, which are absent.
premises: High configurational entropy initially stabilizes a homogeneous solid solution in equiatomic Co–Ni–Cu–Fe–Cr nanoparticles.
At higher temperatures, enthalpy-driven differences in pairwise elemental interactions overcome the entropic stabilization.
This enthalpy-driven effect promotes atomic segregation, especially at surfaces and grain boundaries.
The segregation is more pronounced under reducing atmospheres due to enhanced atomic mobility and altered surface chemistry.
Cu preferentially segregates to surfaces as a specific example of the enthalpy-driven mechanism.
